options.text: Metrics collected from real users' browsers as they use the site
A single scripted test on a fixed device in a lab
The size of the HTML file

questions.explanation: Field data (Real User Monitoring) comes from actual users' browsers, reflecting the real spread of devices, networks, and interactions.

questions.prompt: Match each tool/source to what it is.

pairs.right: A lab audit tool that produces a score and metrics
A lab tool with multi-location waterfalls and filmstrips
A public field dataset reported at the 75th percentile
Your own field RUM measured in real user sessions

questions.explanation: Lighthouse and WebPageTest are lab tools; CrUX and your own web-vitals RUM are field data sources.

questions.prompt: Google's public field dataset from opted-in Chrome users, reported at p75, is the Chrome UX Report, abbreviated ____.
questions.explanation: CrUX (Chrome UX Report) is the public field dataset that powers PageSpeed Insights' field section and Google's page-experience assessment.

questions.prompt: Which statements about LAB data are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: It's great for debugging a cause and for catching regressions in CI
It measures INP directly from real interactions
It's collected from thousands of real users

questions.explanation: Lab data is a repeatable synthetic test, ideal for debugging and CI. It doesn't measure INP directly (no real user) and isn't collected from real users — that's field data.

questions.prompt: Which Core Web Vital can a Lighthouse lab run NOT measure directly, using a proxy instead?

options.text: INP — it uses Total Blocking Time (TBT) as a proxy

questions.explanation: Lighthouse has no real user interacting, so it can't measure INP; it reports TBT as a lab proxy for responsiveness. Confirm INP with field data.

questions.prompt: Order a healthy measure-and-fix workflow using both data types.

items.text: Judge the real experience with field data (p75)
Reproduce and diagnose the cause in the lab
Confirm the improvement later in the field

questions.explanation: Use field data to decide what's actually a problem, lab tools to diagnose and iterate quickly, then confirm the real-world effect back in the field.
